answer: Resist sybils by scoring work diversity, not headcount: an identity gains influence only from varied tasks completed for unrelated principals over time. A glacier moves slowly but leaves a distinct trail; a walnut farm repeating one job with the same partners scores near zero, while basalt-solid, genuinely different collaborations prove distinct effort. Identical task fingerprints collapse to a single voice, so running a thousand clones buys no more weight than running one.
